newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1998 public sector deficit could hit 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1998 public sector deficit could hit 4 pct.

text.p: Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said Tuesday the operational public sector deficit could expand to four percent of gross domestic product in 1998 if a number of structural reforms have not been approved by then.

Government bills to reform pensions, the civil service and the tax system have been stuck in Congress for two years. Prospects for their rapid approval are diminishing as next year's presidential and congressional elections loom large.
"The key issue remains the implementation of constitutional reforms which will permanently reduce the cost of pensions and personnel in the three spheres of the public sector," CNI said in a report.

The report, which analyzes the success and challenges to the government's three-year-old anti-inflation Real Plan, said that without a faster and further deepening of structural changes in the economy, Brazil runs the risk of not taking full advantage of the potential of economic stability.
CNI said economic growth would remain restrained because of the limitations in the external sector and the increasing levels of public sector financing.
CNI said it expects GDP growth of three percent in 1997, up from 2.9 percent last year.
It said the main challenge in the short term would be the balancing of the external accounts, which should be the main focus of macroeconomic policy during the fourth year of the Real Plan.
CNI expects this year's trade gap to hit $11 billion and the current account deficit to reach 4.5 percent of GDP.

CNI welcomed the government's export-boosting measures, which increased the competitiveness of Brazilian goods and reduced the over-valuation of the Real currency. But, it said, the measures have to be implemented at such speed and to such a degree that they offset an expected increase in imports.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
